bibliography.abstract: Refrigerated transport requires distributing products with heterogeneous temperature constraints using vehicles equipped with cooling systems. Beyond traditional routing and capacity decisions, logistics providers must also determine the target temperature inside each vehicle. In this setting, each commodity must be transported within a prescribed temperature interval, so the chosen target temperature directly affects feasibility and determines which commodities can be jointly loaded on a vehicle. We introduce the Multi-Commodity Vehicle Routing Problem with Temperature Requirements (MC-VRP-T) which integrates temperature decisions into the routing process. We study two variants of this problem: (i) a constant-temperature variant, in which each vehicle selects a single temperature that is maintained throughout the route. For this variant, we develop a classical vehicle-indexed formulation and a novel temperature-indexed formulation exploiting an identified structural property, both solved via branch-and-cut, and we further embed this property in a set-partitioning formulation solved with a branch-and-cut-and-price algorithm. (ii) a temperature-adjustable variant, in which a vehicle may adjust its target temperature after each stop. For this more flexible setting, we provide a dedicated mathematical formulation solved via branch-and-cut and compare its complexity and benefits with the constant-temperature variant. The objective in both variants is to jointly determine routes and temperature settings that satisfy commodity-specific temperature requirements while minimizing routing and temperature-related costs. Computational experiments evaluate the performance of the formulations and quantify the economic impact of integrating routing and temperature decisions in refrigerated distribution.

en.caveats: The performance and economic benefits of the proposed formulations are demonstrated through computational experiments rather than a real-world pilot deployment.
en.what: This study introduces the Multi-Commodity Vehicle Routing Problem with Temperature Requirements (MC-VRP-T) to optimize routing alongside vehicle temperature settings for products with diverse thermal constraints. The authors model and solve two operational variants: a constant-temperature model using branch-and-cut and branch-and-cut-and-price algorithms, and a temperature-adjustable model where vehicles can alter their target temperature after deliveries.
en.why: It provides logistics operators with mathematical formulations to simultaneously optimize delivery paths and refrigeration settings, quantifying the cost savings of dynamically adjusting vehicle temperatures versus maintaining a single constant temperature.
